blocks.text: The main difference
blocks.html: The main difference

blocks.text: RabbitMQ queues are a natural fit for routing messages and sharing pending work among workers.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ queues are a natural fit for routing messages and sharing pending work among workers.

blocks.text: Kafka topics are a natural fit for retaining records that independent applications read and replay.
blocks.html: Kafka topics are a natural fit for retaining records that independent applications read and replay.

blocks.text: Both can carry commands and events. “Send an invoice” requests work; “Order placed” reports a fact. The application defines that meaning.
blocks.html: Both can carry commands and events. “Send an invoice” requests work; “Order placed” reports a fact. The application defines that meaning.

blocks.text: The table compares RabbitMQ queues with Kafka topics and traditional consumer groups. Streams and share groups are explained below.
blocks.html: The table compares RabbitMQ queues with Kafka topics and traditional consumer groups. Streams and share groups are explained below.

rows.html: Question
RabbitMQ queues
Kafka topics
Where does data go?
An exchange routes messages to queues.
A producer writes records to topic partitions.
How is work shared?
Consumers on one queue share deliveries.
Consumers in one group share partitions.
How do services each get a copy?
Give each service a separate bound queue.
Give each service a separate consumer group.
How is progress recorded?
Consumers acknowledge deliveries.
Consumers commit the next offset for each partition.
What happens after processing?
Acknowledgement allows removal from that queue.
Reading or committing does not remove records.
Can old data be read again?
Acknowledged messages cannot be replayed from that queue.
Available records can be reread using offsets.
What removes data?
Acknowledgements, expiry, limits, or administrative actions.
Retention, compaction, or administrative actions.
Where are routing rules applied?
Exchanges match keys, patterns, or headers.
Producers select topics and partitions; readers can filter records.
What order is provided?
FIFO delivery, affected by priorities and redelivery.
Record order within each partition; no total order across partitions.
How does reading work?
Usually broker deliveries to subscribed consumers; explicit fetching also exists.
Clients fetch records and track their positions.
How is consumer load controlled?
Prefetch limits unacknowledged deliveries.
Clients control fetching; consumer lag measures how far readers trail the log.
How does processing scale?
Add workers; queue capacity can require more queues.
Add partitions and consumers; active consumers in a traditional group are limited by partition count.

blocks.text: Routing and independent readers
blocks.html: Routing and independent readers

blocks.text: RabbitMQ direct exchanges match a key; topic exchanges match patterns; fanout broadcasts; headers exchanges match attributes.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ direct exchanges match a key; topic exchanges match patterns; fanout broadcasts; headers exchanges match attributes.

blocks.text: One RabbitMQ queue with several workers divides work. Separate queues let services receive independent copies.
blocks.html: One RabbitMQ queue with several workers divides work. Separate queues let services receive independent copies.

blocks.text: Kafka groups read the same stored records independently. A new group can start from available history.
blocks.html: Kafka groups read the same stored records independently. A new group can start from available history.

blocks.text: In both systems, parallel delivery does not guarantee that business actions finish in order.
blocks.html: In both systems, parallel delivery does not guarantee that business actions finish in order.

blocks.text: Failures and delivery guarantees
blocks.html: Failures and delivery guarantees

blocks.text: RabbitMQ: manual acknowledgements allow unfinished deliveries to be redelivered after a consumer disconnects.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ: manual acknowledgements allow unfinished deliveries to be redelivered after a consumer disconnects.

blocks.text: Kafka: a replacement consumer resumes from committed progress. Work completed before a failed commit may repeat.
blocks.html: Kafka: a replacement consumer resumes from committed progress. Work completed before a failed commit may repeat.

blocks.text: Both can lose work with unsafe settings. Both need duplicate-safe processing when retries are possible.
blocks.html: Both can lose work with unsafe settings. Both need duplicate-safe processing when retries are possible.

blocks.text: RabbitMQ publisher confirms report broker acceptance. Consumer acknowledgements report handling; these are separate signals.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ publisher confirms report broker acceptance. Consumer acknowledgements report handling; these are separate signals.

blocks.text: RabbitMQ durability needs suitable queue types, persistence, and confirms. Quorum queues replicate data across brokers.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ durability needs suitable queue types, persistence, and confirms. Quorum queues replicate data across brokers.

blocks.text: Kafka durability depends on replication and producer acknowledgement settings. Retention must cover the required recovery window.
blocks.html: Kafka durability depends on replication and producer acknowledgement settings. Retention must cover the required recovery window.

blocks.text: Replication can preserve availability after some failures. Neither product survives every failure automatically.
blocks.html: Replication can preserve availability after some failures. Neither product survives every failure automatically.

blocks.text: Kafka transactions can commit Kafka output and input offsets together. Correct configuration and recovery are still required.
blocks.html: Kafka transactions can commit Kafka output and input offsets together. Correct configuration and recovery are still required.

blocks.text: Neither product alone makes an external email, payment, or database action happen exactly once.
blocks.html: Neither product alone makes an external email, payment, or database action happen exactly once.

blocks.text: History, replay, and storage
blocks.html: History, replay, and storage

blocks.text: Kafka retention limits how long or how much data remains. Reading does not extend that lifetime.
blocks.html: Kafka retention limits how long or how much data remains. Reading does not extend that lifetime.

blocks.text: Compaction keeps the latest available value for each key over time. It does not preserve every earlier change.
blocks.html: Compaction keeps the latest available value for each key over time. It does not preserve every earlier change.

blocks.text: Replay can use only retained records. A retained log is not automatically a complete audit archive or backup.
blocks.html: Replay can use only retained records. A retained log is not automatically a complete audit archive or backup.

blocks.text: RabbitMQ Streams also retains messages and supports replay. Queue deletion behaviour does not describe every RabbitMQ feature.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ Streams also retains messages and supports replay. Queue deletion behaviour does not describe every RabbitMQ feature.

blocks.text: Kafka share groups let workers share individual records, with acknowledgements. Check broker and client support before choosing this model.
blocks.html: Kafka share groups let workers share individual records, with acknowledgements. Check broker and client support before choosing this model.

blocks.text: Performance and operating cost
blocks.html: Performance and operating cost

blocks.text: Kafka’s batching and partitioned log suit sustained event ingestion and repeated reading.
blocks.html: Kafka’s batching and partitioned log suit sustained event ingestion and repeated reading.

blocks.text: RabbitMQ queues suit routed jobs and individual delivery control. RabbitMQ Streams also supports high-throughput streaming.
blocks.html: RabbitMQ queues suit routed jobs and individual delivery control. RabbitMQ Streams also supports high-throughput streaming.

blocks.text: There is no universal speed winner. Measure latency and throughput with realistic message sizes, durability, and fan-out.
blocks.html: There is no universal speed winner. Measure latency and throughput with realistic message sizes, durability, and fan-out.

blocks.text: Both need storage planning, monitoring, and failure recovery. Slow consumers cause queue backlogs or growing Kafka lag.
blocks.html: Both need storage planning, monitoring, and failure recovery. Slow consumers cause queue backlogs or growing Kafka lag.

blocks.text: A small workflow may not justify a new platform. Existing infrastructure and team experience matter.
blocks.html: A small workflow may not justify a new platform. Existing infrastructure and team experience matter.

blocks.text: Examples: choose by the requirement
blocks.html: Examples: choose by the requirement

blocks.text: Generate PDF reports: RabbitMQ queues
blocks.html: Generate PDF reports: RabbitMQ queues

blocks.text: Need: several workers generate reports; completed jobs need no replay.
blocks.html: Need: several workers generate reports; completed jobs need no replay.

blocks.text: Flow: request → report queue → available worker → save PDF → acknowledge.
blocks.html: Flow: request → report queue → available worker → save PDF → acknowledge.

blocks.text: Why: workers share pending jobs. A stable job ID prevents repeated output after redelivery. Store the PDF outside the queue.
blocks.html: Why: workers share pending jobs. A stable job ID prevents repeated output after redelivery. Store the PDF outside the queue.

blocks.text: Route warehouse jobs: RabbitMQ queues
blocks.html: Route warehouse jobs: RabbitMQ queues

blocks.text: Need: Mumbai jobs go to Mumbai packers; Delhi jobs go to Delhi packers.
blocks.html: Need: Mumbai jobs go to Mumbai packers; Delhi jobs go to Delhi packers.

blocks.text: Flow: exchange → matching warehouse queue → that warehouse’s workers.
blocks.html: Flow: exchange → matching warehouse queue → that warehouse’s workers.

blocks.text: Why: exchange bindings route jobs before delivery. Kafka can use separate topics or application routing, but retained history is not required here.
blocks.html: Why: exchange bindings route jobs before delivery. Kafka can use separate topics or application routing, but retained history is not required here.

blocks.text: Recalculate website metrics: Kafka
blocks.html: Recalculate website metrics: Kafka

blocks.text: Need: analytics, recommendations, and fraud detection share click history.
blocks.html: Need: analytics, recommendations, and fraud detection share click history.

blocks.text: Flow: clicks topic → separate consumer groups. Analytics replays yesterday’s records after a calculation bug.
blocks.html: Flow: clicks topic → separate consumer groups. Analytics replays yesterday’s records after a calculation bug.

blocks.text: Why: one reader can replay without resetting others. Keep the full replay window; compaction would not preserve every click.
blocks.html: Why: one reader can replay without resetting others. Keep the full replay window; compaction would not preserve every click.

blocks.text: Rebuild a search index: Kafka
blocks.html: Rebuild a search index: Kafka

blocks.text: Need: a new index reads product changes while existing readers keep running.
blocks.html: Need: a new index reads product changes while existing readers keep running.

blocks.text: Flow: product changes topic → new index group → retained changes, then live changes.
blocks.html: Flow: product changes topic → new index group → retained changes, then live changes.

blocks.text: Why: a new reader can catch up independently. Keep each product’s changes in one partition and process them sequentially when order matters.
blocks.html: Why: a new reader can catch up independently. Keep each product’s changes in one partition and process them sequentially when order matters.

blocks.text: If history is incomplete, start with a snapshot coordinated with later changes. If a job only scans current database data, a RabbitMQ queue may be enough.
blocks.html: If history is incomplete, start with a snapshot coordinated with later changes. If a job only scans current database data, a RabbitMQ queue may be enough.

blocks.text: Notify two services: existing RabbitMQ
blocks.html: Notify two services: existing RabbitMQ

blocks.text: Need: cache and notification services receive stock changes; neither needs replay.
blocks.html: Need: cache and notification services receive stock changes; neither needs replay.

blocks.text: Flow: exchange → cache queue and notification queue. Each service handles its copy.
blocks.html: Flow: exchange → cache queue and notification queue. Each service handles its copy.

blocks.text: Why: event-driven does not automatically mean Kafka. RabbitMQ already meets this live-delivery requirement.
blocks.html: Why: event-driven does not automatically mean Kafka. RabbitMQ already meets this live-delivery requirement.

blocks.text: If forecasting later needs old changes, evaluate retained history with Kafka or RabbitMQ Streams.
blocks.html: If forecasting later needs old changes, evaluate retained history with Kafka or RabbitMQ Streams.

blocks.text: Order history and invoice jobs: possibly both
blocks.html: Order history and invoice jobs: possibly both

blocks.text: Need: retained order history for independent readers, plus workers generating invoices.
blocks.html: Need: retained order history for independent readers, plus workers generating invoices.

blocks.text: Kafka can retain order events. RabbitMQ can distribute invoice jobs.
blocks.html: Kafka can retain order events. RabbitMQ can distribute invoice jobs.

blocks.text: Why: these are separate needs. Use both only when the benefit justifies operating two systems; one existing platform may suffice.
blocks.html: Why: these are separate needs. Use both only when the benefit justifies operating two systems; one existing platform may suffice.

blocks.text: Use stable operation IDs. Replaying order history must not accidentally resend invoices or repeat payments.
blocks.html: Use stable operation IDs. Replaying order history must not accidentally resend invoices or repeat payments.

blocks.text: Questions that decide the choice
blocks.html: Questions that decide the choice

blocks.text: Is the main need completing pending work, retaining history, or both?
blocks.html: Is the main need completing pending work, retaining history, or both?

blocks.text: Does each service need all records, or should workers divide them?
blocks.html: Does each service need all records, or should workers divide them?

blocks.text: How long must replay work? What ordering and failure recovery are required?
blocks.html: How long must replay work? What ordering and failure recovery are required?

blocks.text: Do routing, retries, priorities, or request–reply matter more than retained history?
blocks.html: Do routing, retries, priorities, or request–reply matter more than retained history?

blocks.text: For request–reply, RabbitMQ supports reply queues and correlation IDs. The application still handles timeouts; Kafka can implement replies too.
blocks.html: For request–reply, RabbitMQ supports reply queues and correlation IDs. The application still handles timeouts; Kafka can implement replies too.

blocks.text: For event sourcing or audit history, verify completeness, retention, deletion rules, and recovery. A product name does not guarantee them.
blocks.html: For event sourcing or audit history, verify completeness, retention, deletion rules, and recovery. A product name does not guarantee them.

blocks.text: Choose the simplest supported setup that meets these requirements, then validate it under realistic load.
blocks.html: Choose the simplest supported setup that meets these requirements, then validate it under realistic load.
